stemBlocks.value: Using a ruler and a pair of compasses only, construct triangle NLM in which LM = 12 cm, ∠MLN = 30° and ∠LMN = 90°.
Think first: The 30° must come from bisecting a constructed 60°, since compasses cannot produce 30° in one step.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p161-q19 from workbook page 161.

solutionSteps.instruction: Construct 60° at L, then bisect it.

contentBlocks.value: 60° arc construction, then equal arcs from the two arc points crossing inside

solutionSteps.instruction: Construct a perpendicular to LM at M, on the same side as the 30° arm.

contentBlocks.value: Equal arcs each side of M, then equal larger arcs crossing above M

solutionSteps.instruction: Mark N where the two arms meet and join LN and MN.

strategyBlocks.value: Draw LM = 12 cm, construct 60° at L and bisect it for 30°, construct the perpendicular at M, and mark N where the two arms meet.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: A correctly constructed triangle NLM with LM = 12 cm, ∠MLN = 30° and ∠LMN = 90°. Accuracy checks: MN ≈ 6.9 cm, LN ≈ 13.9 cm and ∠LNM = 60°.

whyThisWorks.value: Two angles at the ends of a known side determine the triangle, so no further measurement is needed. The construction is exact because 60° comes from an equilateral triangle and bisection halves it precisely; the perpendicular at M is likewise exact, so any error in the finished figure is drawing error, not method error.

commonErrors.misconception: Using a protractor for the 30° when the question says ruler and compasses only.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using a protractor for the 30° when the question says ruler and compasses only.

commonErrors.misconception: Putting the perpendicular on the opposite side of LM from the 30° arm.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Putting the perpendicular on the opposite side of LM from the 30° arm.

commonErrors.misconception: Misreading which vertex each angle belongs to — ∠MLN has its vertex at L.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Misreading which vertex each angle belongs to — ∠MLN has its vertex at L.

examTip.value: Read the vertex order in the angle name carefully: the middle letter is always the vertex, so ∠MLN puts the 30° at L.
